body.statement:
Suppose \(\alpha\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)\), set \(\beta=\alpha/L\), and let \(\eta>0\) be the predeclared rational tolerance.  Then
\[
\Pr\{\Delta_\ell\in I_\ell\text{ for every }1\le\ell\le L\}\ge1-\alpha
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Pr\{\overline\Delta\in\overline I\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
There exists a finite constant \(C_\alpha\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed role-share bounds, such that
\[
\mathbb E\{\operatorname{diam}(\overline I)\}
\le C_\alpha\left\{\frac{\max(1,\sqrt{n\rho})}{n}+\eta\right\}.
\]
body.justification: The fixed fifteen-pair target needs simultaneous rather than pointwise validity before interval averaging.
body.gap: The published block bootstrap aggregates interior influence functions and does not guarantee finite-sample coverage at zero counts.
body.consumer: The Buenos Aires-style fifteen-comparison DTT aggregate receives one causal-scale interval with a transparent multiplicity correction.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and \(1\leq \ell\leq L\), and put
\[
p_{\ell}=(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3},r_{\ell4}).
\]
By the common-rarity assumption, \(p_{\ell j}=\rho c_{\ell j}\).  The coefficient box and rarity-scale assumptions imply
\[
0<p_{\ell j}\leq 4\rho\leq \frac14.
\]
Moreover, for every \(i,j\in J\),
\[
\frac{p_{\ell i}}{p_{\ell j}}
=\frac{c_{\ell i}}{c_{\ell j}}
\leq \frac{4}{1/2}=8.
\]
Thus \(p_{\ell}\in\mathcal P_0\).  By the published identification proposition and the definition of \(G\),
\[
\Delta_{\ell}
=H(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3})-r_{\ell4}
=G(p_{\ell}).
\tag{1}
\]
This step relates the causal contrast \(\Delta_{\ell}\) to the observed-law functional \(G\); it does not define the former as the latter.

Set \(\beta=\alpha/L\).  Since \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(L=15\), one has \(0<\beta<1\); since \(\alpha\) is rational, so is \(\beta\).  We next verify that the coverage and diameter conclusions of the rational outer-interval argument apply for every positive rational \(\eta\), including \(\eta>1/n\).  This avoids invoking the stated pairwise theorem outside its displayed range.

For one pair, abbreviate \(n_j=n_{\ell j}\), \(K_j=K_{\ell j,n}\), \(x_j=K_j/n_j\), and \(M_n=\sum_{j=1}^4n_j\).  In the rational algorithm, the likelihood threshold \(t_{\rm lo}\) is strictly positive.  For every \(\eta>0\), there exists a positive rational mesh \(h\) satisfying
\[
M_nh\leq t_{\rm lo}/4,
\qquad
L_{\rm lip}h\leq\eta/8.
\tag{2}
\]
Hence the finite construction and its deterministic image-containment argument remain valid without the restriction \(\eta\leq1/n\): every \(p\in\mathcal R_\beta(K)\) lies in a retained feasible box, and the global Lipschitz enlargement and outward rounding give
\[
G\{\mathcal R_\beta(K)\}
\subseteq \mathsf{Outer}_{\beta,\eta}(K).
\tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the likelihood Lipschitz inequality used by that construction is
\[
|L_K(p)-L_K(p')|\leq M_n\lVert p-p'\rVert_\infty,
\]
so the first inequality in (2) ensures retention, while the second bounds the image enlargement.  Neither step requires an upper bound on \(\eta\).

Under Bernoulli role sampling and disjoint-role independence, the four counts for this pair are independent binomials with parameters \((n_j,p_{\ell j})\).  For \(0<p_{ell j}<1\), the elementary Bernoulli-divergence bound gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left\{\operatorname{Bern}(x_j),
\operatorname{Bern}(p_{\ell j})\right\}
\leq \frac{(x_j-p_{\ell j})^2}
{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})}.
\]
Because
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}(x_j-p_{\ell j})^2
=\frac{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})}{n_j},
\]
the definition of the deviance yields
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}D_{p_\ell}(K)
\leq 2\sum_{j=1}^4 n_j
\frac{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})/n_j}
{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})}
=8.
\tag{4}
\]
Markov's inequality, the definition of \(\mathcal R_\beta\), and (3) therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_{p_\ell}\{G(p_\ell)\notin I_\ell\}
&\leq \Pr_{p_\ell}\{p_\ell\notin\mathcal R_\beta(K)\}\\
&=\Pr_{p_\ell}\{D_{p_\ell}(K)>8/\beta\}\\
&\leq \beta=\frac{\alpha}{L}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

For completeness, the diameter calculation also remains valid for arbitrary \(\eta>0\).  Put \(q'=8/\beta+2\log4\).  The likelihood-threshold and mesh inequalities in (2) imply that every feasible point in a retained box belongs to
\[
\mathcal R'(K)=\{p\in\mathcal P_0:D_p(K)\leq q'\}.
\]
The Hellinger lower bound for Bernoulli divergence then gives, for \(p\in\mathcal R'(K)\),
\[
|\sqrt{p_j}-\sqrt{x_j}|
\leq \sqrt{\frac{q'}{2n_j}}.
\tag{6}
\]
Consequently, for any \(p,p'\in\mathcal R'(K)\),
\[
|p_j-p'_j|
\leq 4\sqrt{x_j}\sqrt{\frac{q'}{2n_j}}
+\frac{2q'}{n_j}.
\tag{7}
\]
The global Lipschitz bound, the enlargement in (2), and the final outward rounding therefore give a finite constant \(C_{0,\beta}\), independent of \(\ell,n,\rho,c\), such that
\[
\operatorname{diam}(I_\ell)
\leq C_{0,\beta}
\left\{
\sum_{j=1}^4\left(\sqrt{\frac{x_j}{n_j}}+\frac1{n_j}\right)+\eta
\right\}.
\tag{8}
\]
If the retained list is empty, the returned interval is \([0,0]\), so (8) is still true.  Jensen's inequality, common rarity, the coefficient upper bound, and the lower role-share bound give
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}\sqrt{x_j}
\leq\sqrt{p_{\ell j}}
\leq2\sqrt\rho,
\qquad
n_j\geq\underline\pi n.
\tag{9}
\]
Taking expectations in (8) and using (9), uniformly over the fixed pairs, produces a finite constant \(C_\beta\), depending only on \(\beta\) and the fixed role-share bounds (with the fixed Lipschitz certificate absorbed), for which
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}\{\operatorname{diam}(I_\ell)\}
\leq C_\beta\left\{
\sqrt{\frac\rho n}+\frac1n+\eta
\right\}
\leq C_\beta\left\{
\frac{\max(1,\sqrt{n\rho})}{n}+\eta
\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus both conclusions needed below hold for every positive rational \(\eta\).

Let \(A_\ell=\{\Delta_\ell\notin I_\ell\}\).  Cross-pair independence is unnecessary: by (1), (5), and the union bound,
\[
\Pr\{\Delta_\ell\in I_\ell\text{ for every }1\leq\ell\leq L\}
=1-\Pr\!\left(\bigcup_{\ell=1}^L A_\ell\right)
\geq1-\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Pr(A_\ell)
\geq1-L\frac{\alpha}{L}
=1-\alpha.
\tag{11}
\]
Write \(I_\ell=[L_\ell,U_\ell]\).  On the simultaneous event in (11),
\[
L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L L_\ell
\leq L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Delta_\ell
=\overline\Delta
\leq L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L U_\ell.
\]
By the definition of \(\overline I\), this is precisely \(\overline\Delta\in\overline I\), and hence
\[
\Pr\{\overline\Delta\in\overline I\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{12}
\]
Finally, the same definition gives the deterministic identity
\[
\operatorname{diam}(\overline I)
=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\operatorname{diam}(I_\ell).
\tag{13}
\]
Taking expectations in (13), applying (10) to each of the fixed \(L=15\) pairs, and setting \(C_\alpha=C_{\alpha/L}\) proves
\[
\mathbb E\{\operatorname{diam}(\overline I)\}
\leq C_\alpha\left\{
\frac{\max(1,\sqrt{n\rho})}{n}+\eta
\right\}.
\]
